facts.fact_text: The first applicant is a political activist.
The second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh applicants are political activists.
On 24 November 2007 a group of opposition politicians organised protest rallies in several Russian cities, including Moscow.
On 24 November 2007 the applicants attended a gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt.
The gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt on 24 November 2007 had been organised by the second applicant.

According to the applicants, at 3 p.m. on 24 November 2007, at the end of the gathering on Academician Sakharov Prospekt, the applicants started walking to the location of another authorised gathering on Chistoprudnyy Boulevard.
The applicants' route on 24 November 2007 was blocked by the riot police.
The applicants' route on 24 November 2007 was blocked by the riot police.
The applicants were arrested on 24 November 2007.
The first applicant was charged with breaching the established procedure for conducting public events, an offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The first applicant was charged with disobeying lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant was charged with breaching the established procedure for conducting public events, an offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant was charged with disobeying lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
A summary of the relevant domestic law is contained in Kasparov and Others v. Russia (no. 21613/07, § 35, 3 October 2013).
A summary of the relevant domestic law is contained in Navalnyy and Yashin v. Russia (no. 76204/11, §§ 43-44, 4 December 2014).
The first applicant was charged with breaching the established procedure for conducting public events, an offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The first applicant was charged with disobeying lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant was charged with breaching the established procedure for conducting public events, an offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant was charged with disobeying lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicants' route on 24 November 2007 was blocked by the riot police.
Excessive force was allegedly used against the applicants at the time of their arrest on 24 November 2007.

The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow established that the first applicant had marched among some 1,500 people in what had constituted an unauthorised public event on 24 November 2007.
The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow based her findings on police officers M. and U.'s witness statements and written reports.
The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow based her findings on the administrative offence statements in respect of two charges against the first applicant.

The Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow dismissed the first applicant's testimony as false, finding that it contradicted the police officers' testimony and reports.
According to the first applicant, members of the public who wanted to attend the hearing of his case were prevented from entering the court on 24 November 2007.
According to the first applicant, the court had been cordoned off by the riot police on 24 November 2007.

The first applicant claimed that even his lawyers had experienced difficulties getting into the court of the Justice of the Peace of Circuit no. 382 of the Krasnoselskiy District of Moscow on 24 November 2007.
